#2769. Vikings' 17:28 time of possession was their lowest in franchise history

The Minnesota Vikings have played 1,064 games in the history of their franchise, which started in 1961. Before yesterday, they had never played a game in which they possessed the ball for less than 17 and a half minutes. Now they have.

The Vikings’ time of possession of 17:28 in Monday night’s 23-6 loss to the Bills was their lowest in franchise history.

The previous franchise low was 17:38, set in the NFC Championship Game after the 2000 season, when the Vikings lost to the Giants 41-0.

On Monday night, the Vikings’ offense could not stay on the field. The first quarter set the tone: They had three possessions, which were two three-and-outs and one possession on which they lost a fumble on the first play. Their longest possession of the night lasted 3:11, and on that possession they ran five plays, totaled just 10 yards, and punted.

The Vikings’ defense played well, but not so well that the Bills weren’t able to sustain some long drives, including three drives that took more than six minutes off the clock. The Bills gained 22 first downs; the Vikings gained just nine.

The Bills’ 42:32 time of possession was their second-best in franchise history, trailing only a 1989 game in which they possessed the ball for 42:53 and beat the Jets 34-3.

#2768. Charge want to be a pipeline for the Cavs: ‘We want the development to be in-house’

CLEVELAND — The G League matters more for team building than ever. Look no further than the Cleveland Cavaliers roster for proof.

Seven of the 14 players on standard deals for the Cavs have spent time in the G League. That number should jump to eight, with Khalifa Diop expecting to play with the Cleveland Charge some this year as well. Diop's inclusion would mean that over half the roster has spent time in the G League.

This is a change from where things were over a decade ago. The reasons for that are layered. Investment in the league, along with changes to the salary cap and the style of play, has all contributed to this.

"In the world of aprons and salary cap and all this, what better way to cultivate the next wave of people that can help fit into [an NBA] environment than this?" Charge head coach Eli Kell-Abrams said.

The Cavs have invested in the Charge over the last several seasons. The move from Canton to Cleveland has allowed them to use the Cavs' training facility. More recently, switching their home games to Cleveland Public Auditorium, along with refitting the building for basketball, speaks to the organization's commitment to the G League.

"We want the development to be in-house," Charge general manager Liron Fanan said. "The type of players that you now take on your G League team, you really take into consideration what Kenny [Atkinson] and his staff are looking for. What kind of player are they on and off the court? How can he fit our culture of the Cavs and what we're looking for? It's mainly guys that are willing to accept a role, willing to compete every day, work hard, put their head down, and be ready."

The Charge are looking to identify and develop role players who can specifically fit alongside the Cavs' core group. There are two skills that the Charge are looking to cultivate, knowing that they will translate to the next level.

"They're going to have to be defensively minded, and also able to make shots when you stand in the corner because you're not going to have the ball in your hands," Fanan said. "You're going to be that guy that comes off the bench for five minutes and tries to impact the game in those minutes. So, how ready are you? What's your mentality? The toughness and the willingness to just take a role. Those are the skills that we look at."

The Charge are trying to refine those skills with their two-way players. Riley Minix has proven to be a good shooter — Summer League notwithstanding — but shooting alone isn't going to allow him to become a rotation player. "He needs to get better [defensively]," Fanan said. "Can he really defend and switch at the NBA level? We saw a little bit of that, and we're seeing improvement. I think there needs to be a big jump this year."

Rookie two-way center Ernest Udeh Jr. has the potential to develop into a useful backup center. The Cavs like the motor, but there's a learning curve for bigs transitioning from college to the pros.

"He always plays hard, now for us, it's to get him better at understanding spacing," Fanan said. "Understanding guarding outside the perimeter, working with his hands better."

Success in the G League is different than the NBA. The Charge want to win games, but their goal is to ensure they're developing talent that can be used by the Cavs and other NBA teams. For them to continue doing that, they want to continue cultivating a culture that makes that possible.

"We're in a league that is sometimes not about the right stuff," Kell-Abrams said. "We want to be the group that relies on each other, that is about everybody else's success. That passed the ball in a league that doesn't."

The Charge open their season at home on Tuesday night against the Motor City Cruise.

“You’ve seen it done so many ways, right? So many different examples of it being done,” Coen said. “I know he’s pretty intelligent, and he’ll be able to understand a lot of that. Like our verbiage where I would imagine three, cover three, cover four, you know, like the coverages, he’ll understand and know and be able to play those, line up and play. It’s more of the checks and balances and things that go into each play that we’ll have to work through. We’ll take it one day at a time, see what happens.”

#2762. Davis puts on a show, Dybantsa flashes potential in loss to Pistons

The Washington Wizards got 44 points and 13 rebounds from Anthony Davis, and very little from anyone else, and lost to the Detroit Pistons, 122-111.

It was Washington's fourth straight loss as the team has struggled to generate effective offense or maintain stout defense.

Davis put on a show, especially in the first half, dominating the center-less Detroit lineup. He scored 30 points in the first half on 10-11 shooting from the floor. The Wizards headed to the locker room down 10 because the rest of the team shot 10-30.

AJ Dybantsa shows big time potential in Wizards loss to the Detroit Pistons. | Getty Images

For the game, Davis shot 16-21. The rest of the team: 25-68. Davis used 25 offensive possessions to generate 41 points. His teammates used 78 possessions to produce 70 points. As the great Fred Katz used to say, "Yikes guys."

The other major redeeming feature of the game was the play of No. 1 overall pick AJ Dybantsa, who had the most spectacular replacement level game I've ever seen. I can't decide which plays impressed me the most:

The lightning Euro-step drive in transition that froze John Collins and ended with a two-handed dunk

The drive that included getting fouled by Cade Cunningham out top, and ended with a cuffed dunk on Collins

The fake drive to attack a closeout that led to a relocation stepback three from the corner

That doesn't include his relentless defensive effort and the constant pressure he put on the Detroit defense. Or his duel with Cunningham that was massively entertaining.

Or when he battled Ron Holland for a loose ball, inadvertently slapped him in the face, and then spent a chunk of the break while refs watched the replay reviewing the play on the arena screen with Detroit's Daniss Jenkins.

The five turnovers and below average turnovers undermined his overall value for the game, but the highlights were big time plays, and the defensive impact was great from a 19-year-old rookie.

The Peacock broadcast format is great, and I hope it catches on around the league. Embedding the analysts on the benches is a genius innovation — especially when they share what the coaches are telling their players.

Bilal Coulibaly missed the game with a left hand injury that I'm pretty sure happened a couple games ago.

Will Riley entered the game in the first half, and almost immediately gave up one of the easiest drives in Cunningham's career. Zero resistance. Not even turnstile level defense.

Around 8:41 in the second quarter, Davis got an open three because Trae Young sprinted off screens, turned the corner and got into the paint. His effort on the play forced the help defender to commit (not coming over would have conceded a layup), which left Davis wide open at the three-point line. Young made the pass, and Davis converted.

When I looked at my notes, I discovered one more Dybantsa play that I'd forgotten — in the second quarter, he threw a fake so fast and convincing that Kevin Huerter stepped in the wrong direction. Dybantsa went past him for a layup.

Detroit opened the second half with Duncan Robinson getting a four-point play on what I thought was a bad call on Young. The Wizards started the period with a turnover, and then followed it up with an atrocious possession that ended with Dybantsa being forced to take a deep three with the shot clock running out. The team had tried — and failed — to feed Kyshawn George in the post against the diminutive Jenkins. They then ran multiple screens that finally got a switch that gave Dybantsa a mismatch…and not enough time to attack it.

Peaccock's Austin Rivers reported that during a third quarter timeout, Wizards coach Brian Keefe urged the team to improve their effort. His critique included Davis, who'd just given up a backcut dunk to Cunningham, which included an and-one free throw. "Let's not wait until the next game," Keefe said, according to Rivers. "Let's do it now."

George needs to figure out to play on offense without turning it over so much. He had five more turnovers last night. On one in the fourth quarter, he drove into the paint, couldn't get to the rim, and picked up his dribble. Stuck, and with the three-second count ticking, he attempted a ridiculous pass out with Ausar Thompson in the vicinity. The pass was stolen, of course.

I wrote this in the fourth quarter, but I could have written it in any period: The Wizards cannot figure out how to initiate their offense. Dybantsa set a screen for George. George came up to set a ball screen for Davis. But, Davis went nowhere. George drifted a little and the possession just stalled. Davis finally tossed up a three, which missed. The offensive design was fine, though perhaps not with Davis as the ball handler.

A few minutes later, the Wizards ran a similar set but with Davis screening for George. Davis rolled hard, George made a crisp pass, and Davis converted the layup.

Thompson had an amazing block on Alex Sarr with around four minutes left in the game. He met Sarr at the rim, contested with with verticality, went up higher despite being several inches smaller, and swatted the dunk attempt.

Below are the four factors that decide wins and losses in basketball — shooting (efg), rebounding (offensive rebounds), ball handling (turnovers), fouling (free throws made).

eFG% (effective field goal percentage, which accounts for the three-point shot)

TOV% (turnover percentage — turnovers divided by possessions)

FTM/FGA (free throws made divided by field goal attempts)

PPA is my overall production metric, which credits players for things they do that help a team win (scoring, rebounding, playmaking, defending) and dings them for things that hurt (missed shots, turnovers, bad defense, fouls).

PPA is a per possession metric designed for larger data sets. In small sample sizes, the numbers can get weird. In PPA, 100 is average, higher is better and replacement level is 45. For a single game, replacement level isn't much use, and I reiterate the caution about small samples sometimes producing weird results.

POSS is the number of possessions each player was on the floor in this game.

ORTG = offensive rating, which is points produced per individual possessions x 100. League average so far this season is listed in the Four Factors table above. Points produced is not the same as points scored. It includes the value of assists and offensive rebounds, as well as sharing credit when receiving an assist.

USG = offensive usage rate. Average is 20%. Median last season was 17.7%.

ORTG and USG are versions of stats created by former Wizards assistant coach Dean Oliver and modified by me. ORTG is an efficiency measure that accounts for the value of shooting, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers. USG includes shooting from the floor and free throw line, offensive rebounds, assists and turnovers.

+PTS = "Plus Points" is a measure of the points gained or lost by each player based on their efficiency in this game compared to league average efficiency on the same number of possessions. A player with an offensive rating (points produced per possession x 100) of 100 who uses 20 possessions would produce 20 points. If the league average efficiency is 115, the league — on average — would produced 23.0 points in the same 20 possessions. So, the player in this hypothetical would have a +PTS score of -3.0.

Players are sorted by total production in the game.

#2758. Wemby is an alien; Phoenix is painfully human

There were no illusions of grandeur entering the Suns' matchup against the San Antonio Spurs on Monday night. The game would serve as a litmus test, an opportunity to see where Phoenix stood against one of the best teams in the NBA, and it played out pretty much as you might have expected. The Spurs are one of those unique teams that have the advantage of youth on their side, and when you add the fact that they have an alien in Victor Wembanyama patrolling both ends of the floor, defeating them is going to be a difficult task for every team across the Association throughout the season.

Victor Wembanyama is a demigod, an unstoppable force who, at this point, is toying with the sport of basketball. His impact on both ends of the floor is unlike anything we've seen. He possesses the size of Shawn Bradley, whom many of us grew up watching, but his game extends far beyond simply being big. The way he defends, the way he deters anyone who ventures inside the three-point arc, and the constant threat of his mere existence manipulate the game in a manner that leaves you shrugging your shoulders and sighing.

As for the Suns? They did a good job taking care of the basketball, committing only seven turnovers. But they were outscored 62-48 in the paint, 20-10 in second-chance points, and 19-10 in fast-break points. They were also outrebounded by 20, with San Antonio holding a commanding 55-35 advantage on the glass.

The Suns have made progress over the past week, but there's still a considerable gap between where they are and where the Western Conference's elite reside. San Antonio exposed the same deficiencies we've been discussing all season, particularly Phoenix's inability to control the glass and protect the paint. There's no shame in losing to a team featuring a generational talent like Wembanyama. But the manner in which you lose can tell you plenty about how far you still have to go.

It's not often the guy who scores under 10 points gets the Bright Side Baller, but the community here knows ball. The impact Ryan Dunn had in the victory over the Rockets was stellar, as he was a disruptor in every sense of the word.

#2754. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2752. Warriors have won eight straight games after blowing out Pelicans

SAN FRANCISCO – It might be too premature, but the Golden State Warriors look like one of the best teams in the Western Conference, let alone the NBA.

The early results indicate that at the very least, they are one of the hottest in the association. The Warriors have won eight straight games after blowing out the New Orleans Pelicans, 138-87, at Chase Center in San Francisco on Monday, Nov. 9. Stephen Curry and Brandin Podziemski each scored 25 points.

Golden State extended their win streak to eight games and advanced to 8-3 after an 0-3 start to the season which caused many to panic. Guard De'Anthony Melton told USA TODAY Sports for a split moment the team was in a "dark place" after the slow start.

"We knew we couldn't win games and stuff like that," Melton said after scoring 16 points in the win. "Nobody wants to see 0-3, but at the same time I think after we lost our third one, the next day the vibes were still high. Like we were 0-3 but we're still just enjoying being around, having fun, playing cards, stuff like that."

There was additional outside noise, chatter of where the Warriors might finish. They were already counted out to begin the year, projected to finish 41-41. When they got off to the 0-3 start, that's all they heard.

"It's hard not to hear it, but you don't ever play into it," Curry told USA TODAY Sports. "I know I've seen some memes with the towel over my head, staring into the distance, trying to figure out what, you know, we needed to do.  People put an existential crisis on those looks. We hate losing. So you want to respond to all of that.  You hear it, but, we've been around long enough to know, you gotta be able to block all that stuff out, just be who you are."

Everyone outside of the Bay Area might be surprised at the Warriors hot start. But within the team, they remained calm and poised. There was a needed regroup that contributed to their hot streak.

"We're doing all the things we need to to convince ourselves that we are the team we think we can (be)," Curry said. "You know, starting 0-3, like, nobody's panicking, but it's still a feeling that you don't like where you haven't been rewarded for the effort that you're putting in."

The jury is still out on whether the Warriors are turning the page to becoming a great team, but Curry likes the direction they're heading in.

"My take is that we're a very resilient team and that matters to become part of a good, maybe a great team down the stretch of the year," Curry said. "If you can withstand some rough nights, whether shooting the ball, turnovers, or whatever, still find a way to win... I'm proud of everything we're doing. We just gotta keep it going."

More: Warriors backcourt depth takes hit losing Brandon Williams, Will Richard

There have been enough games to have a sample size of the Warriors' potential. Their first three games weren't enough to write them off, but they did display some fixable bad habits. One of their main concerns was taking care of the basketball. The Warriors turned the ball over 45 times in their first three games of the season.

Forward Draymond Green was asked to assess where the team is at through 10 games. Green told USA TODAY Sports he'd give them a "B" grade.

"I think we have a lot of things we can get better at. We're still not quite where we want to be, as far as turning the ball over," Green said. "We're executing better, but the execution isn't where we want it to be. Defensively, we've gotten a lot better since game one. That's been kind of our calling card right now and allowing us to win these games."

"A lot of room for growth, but yeah, no one's complaining, either," he added. "We're pretty… excited about where we are as a team, but it's equally as exciting (that) we have so much room to grow."

The Warriors don't look like the same team that began 0-3. They've since cleaned up their game and put attention into the small details of the game.

Head coach Steve Kerr discussed the goal of being a top-10 team in both offense and defense. It's one of the traits that makes a championship team.

Golden State currently ranks 3rd in defensive rating (103.5) in the early 2026–27 NBA season, according to NBA Advanced Leaders.

"The whole thing is about our process," Kerr told USA TODAY Sports. "Can we take care of the ball?  Can we execute offensively, get good shots for each other? And then defend like we have been in recent games, taking care of transition defense, taking away the easy stuff. So, it's not magic. We have a formula, and we're trying to get the guys to play to that formula, that standard night in and night out. We're on a good path, but this will be a great test for us on this road trip, so we'll see how we can do it."

Golden State has to lean into a team identity where there's a reliance upon every player, 1 through 15, to be ready when their name is called. The Warriors suffered losses to Brandon Williams and Will Richard, who will both seemingly be out for some time.

"We got guys that have been around the league, we always want to encourage them, if somebody's down, be ready to play," Melton said. "No matter what, it's the NBA, and we're trying to win games as a team because at the end of the day when we hold up the trophy, that's for everybody. So I think it's always going to be next man up."

Melton added that Curry, Green and Al Horford have breathed confidence into whoever is coming in the game to make an impact.

"(Curry) spoke to the team after the game (against the Magic) about the contributions of the bench," Kerr said. "He mentioned how much trust that he and the vets have in the young guys, and so we've got a good thing going. We've got a good vibe. Guys are all competing for each other. Playing really hard."

Offensively, the Warriors rank 5th in the NBA in offensive rating at 116.7 points per 100 possessions early in the season. They are led by Curry, their longtime superstar, but rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is making his imprint on the team as well, averaging 21.4 points and 7.2 rebounds.

"Our second best player right now is a rookie," Green said about Lendeborg. "He's gonna continue to get better. And as you can see, how good he's already made us, as he gets better, we'll continue to get better. But I think we got a lot of room for growth, and that's exciting."

This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Warriors have won eight straight games after blowing out Pelicans

#2749. Hawkeyes Look to Take Care of Business Against Purdue

That road trip could not have gone much better.

Iowa walked into the shiny, new home of the Northwestern Wildcats, Ryan Field, on Saturday night and decided to do some redecorating. The Hawkeye defense sacked Nicco Marchiol six times and held the Wildcats to 1-of-11 on third down. L.J. Phillips Jr. ran for a career-best 128 yards in his first start and Braeden Jackson housed a kickoff 96 yards for his second return touchdown of the season. Iowa walked out with a 24-10 win that never felt that close, making it five straight over Northwestern.

The Hawkeyes move to 7-2 with a two-game winning streak and what feels like a whole lot of momentum as the schedule turns toward home.

Hank Brown keeps stacking efficient football too. Saturday's line was modest, 16-of-21 for 126 yards with a touchdown and a pick, plus a 21-yard scoring run on a quarterback draw, but he has completed 80% of his throws over the last two games and his 65.8% season mark would be the best by an Iowa quarterback since at least 2013. For the Wisconsin shutout the Big Ten named him Offensive Player of the Week and the quarterback question that consumed October is pretty clearly a settled matter, regardless of what the depth chart may say.

Which brings us to the part nobody in Iowa City wants to jinx: the playoff path is, somehow, still alive – however slim it may be. AP voters jumped Iowa five spots to #16 with the Coaches Poll a tick higher at #15 after the road win over the Wildcats. The second CFP rankings arrive Tuesday night with the Hawkeyes expected to climb similarly from their #19 debut. They're not going to be in at this point, but losses in front of them have left the door open. Lose any of the remaining three games and the door again slams shut.

As of Monday evening, ahead of that second set of playoff rankings, the Hawkeyes had the 16th best odds to make the CFP at +220. That's just over a 31% chance to win all three games and get some help in front of them. Oddsmakers see the first of those as the easy part. FanDuel Sportsbook opened with Iowa as 16.5-favorites against Northwestern and that number had crept to -17.5 by Monday evening with an over/under of 47.5 total points, giving us an implied final in the neighborhood of 32-15.

Purdue is 3-6 (2-4), riding a three-game losing streak and coming off a weekend that cost a coach his job. Less than 24 hours after a 34-29 Homecoming loss to Maryland, Barry Odom fired defensive coordinator Kevin Kane on Sunday morning, nine games into Kane's second stint running Purdue's defense. It's not a huge surprise with numbers like these: #124 nationally in scoring defense at 32.3 points a game, #123 in total defense, #116 against the pass and #99 against the run, with bottom-10 marks on third down and in the red zone. Odom hasn't named a replacement and wouldn't even say who will call the defense Saturday, telling reporters he'd let them know after the game. Iowa gets the first crack at a defense that is somewhere between wounded and leaderless.

There has been real progress in West Lafayette this year, to be fair. Odom inherited a 2-10 trainwreck and this team already snapped an 18-game Big Ten losing streak at Illinois. They also hung 41 on the same Minnesota team that we thought killed Iowa's playoff hopes earlier this year.

The Boilermaker offense is legitimately dangerous through the air: Purdue ranks #26 nationally in passing at 267 yards a game behind Ryan Browne, who has thrown for 2,260 yards with 11 touchdowns and only 5 picks after shaking the turnover bug that defined his 2025. Asaad Waseem is a real weapon and his 709 receiving yards rank among the Big Ten's best. The Boilers really struggle on the ground, though. Purdue runs it at 3.5 a carry, #117 nationally. Purdue can throw it on just about anybody and to this point, run it on nobody.

Iowa's profile remains the photographic negative. After giving up just 10 points on 286 yards to Northwestern, the defense is top-10 nationally in four categories: #3 in scoring at 12.2 points allowed, #5 against the run at 81.9 yards (with two rushing touchdowns allowed all season), #9 in total defense and #7 in sacks with 30. The three shutouts are Iowa's most since 1997. The soft spots are familiar – a #103 passing offense, 27.8 points a game and a turnover margin that sits at minus-1. But this offense has scored enough in every game the defense has kept close save Minnesota and it just went on the road and won by two scores without cracking 300 total yards.

Sacks, in both directions. Iowa has 30 on the year and has allowed just 8, both top-10 marks nationally. Purdue has 11 and has allowed 24.

That's the whole game in one line of the stat sheet. Browne is a rhythm passer who has cleaned up his turnover problem, but he has struggled when opponents have been able to get home. In Purdue's three wins (against Indiana State, Illinois and Minnesota), opponents have combined for just two sacks. That leaves a staggering 22 sacks allowed in the six losses – 3.7 per game.

For Browne, specifically, the splits in wins and losses are staggering. He's completing 69% of his passes at 9.1 yards per attempt with 5 TDs and no interceptions in those three wins. In the six losses, the completion percentage dips to just under 60% with 7.4 yards per attempt while he has only six TDs to five interceptions in those matchups.

Flip it over and Purdue's pass rush generates barely one sack a game against an Iowa line that allows under one. If Brown gets clean pockets against the country's #116 pass defense while Browne spends the night under duress, the two-plus-touchdown spread will look conservative.

Purdue's one path is the turnover column: Iowa sits at minus-1 there, Purdue at plus-2 and giveaways are the only currency that could close a 20-point gap in scoring defense. Pressure on the QB is the surest way to generate turnovers.

Here's a quick look at the details for Saturday.

Date: Saturday, November 14Time: 6:35 pm CTMatchup: Purdue Boilermakers (3-6, 2-4) at #16 Iowa Hawkeyes (7-2, 4-2)Location: Kinnick Stadium – Iowa City, IowaTV: NBCInitial Weather Forecast: Sunny day, kickoff temps in the mid 40s falling into the 30s with light windsFanDuel Opening Line: Iowa -17.5 O/U 47.5

Saturday will mark the 95th meeting between these programs and here's a not so fun fact that surprises most people under 60: Purdue leads the all-time series 50-41-3. The Boilermakers owned this matchup for generations and have stayed annoying long after the series flipped – 38-36 in 2018, 24-20 in 2020 and the one burned into recent memory: the 2021 ambush at Kinnick when unranked Purdue intercepted four passes and stunned #2 Iowa 24-7.

That 2021 game is still Purdue's last win in the series and its last in Kinnick. Iowa took the last two meetings in 2022 and 2023 before the schedule rotation gave everyone a two-year breather, so this is the first look at Odom's version of the Boilermakers. Regardless of who is coming to town, November at Kinnick has been nearly automatic. Iowa has won 24 of its last 29 November home games and eight straight at night in its own building. Saturday is a night kick and the Military Appreciation game and the Hawks haven't lost a game when favored by two TDs since 2016.

To that end, Iowa has won 88% of their games when favored by at least two TDs under Ferentz. They're 7-3 in Kinnick in the month of November when favored by 14+. However, the Hawkeyes have long loved the rock fight and while they rarely lose games where they're favored big, they cover even less often. In that same 10-game span of November games in Kinnick when favored by 14+, Iowa is just 2-8 against the spread.

So buckle up, this one could be tigher than we'd like.

#2747. NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 10

A defensive effort in which the Bills stopped the Vikings' Carson Wentz-led offense, while Josh Allen and the offense did enough to secure a pivotal road victory against Minnesota.

Caleb Williams started in his typical efficient self, and it looked like he could do no wrong, but then he proceeded to throw four interceptions, and the Bears' offense stagnated for much of the game after taking a 17-3 lead. The Buccaneers made the game interesting, forcing five turnovers, but Chicago held strong and defeated Tampa Bay, 27-24.

Brock Purdy went 17 of 25 for 232 yards with a pair of touchdowns to help the 49ers defeat the Las Vegas Raiders, 38-17. The Raiders kept the game interesting up until about half-time, but the 49ers scored two touchdowns in the third quarter to pull away from the Raiders. The defense forced an insane five turnovers. San Francisco remains a top team in the NFL.

Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the NFL, but they faced a Joe Fagnano's Ravens team that only scored 10 points. Jacksonville won the game 33-10 and Trevor Lawrence only completed 16 passes. The Jaguars are an excellent young football team playing complementary football.

Denver found a way to earn a tough road win, again! Pat Bryant returned from IR and caught a touchdown from Bo Nix. Jonah Coleman continues to dominate touches as the team's No. 1 back. Coleman had 17 carries for 57 yards and a touchdown in the game.

The Bengals offense is playing very well. Joe Burrow tossed three touchdowns and 271 yards against the Falcons. Ja'Marr Chase caught ten passes for 155 yards with a touchdown. The rushing attack is still a work in progress for Cincinnati, but the Bengals have now won four games in a row, scoring over 30 points in each matchup.

The Minnesota Vikings battled the Bills but lost at home to Josh Allen. The Carson Wentz experience was not enjoyable, as he threw several interceptions and could not move the offense. Minnesota still has the best defense — and possibly the best unit overall — but this offense is bad.

Kansas City got right against the Jets in a 35-12 victory. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards with a pair of touchdowns, and Kenneth Walker III rushed for over 100 yards with both receiving touchdowns. The Chiefs dominated an inferior opponent.

Detroit went into Miami and won a gritty game that relied on defensive football. Each team turned the football over once, and neither team earned 300 yards on offense. Kudos to Miami's defense, but the Dolphins were a fish out of water for the Lions in Miami.

The Green Bay Packers demolished the New England Patriots in their home. They forced four turnovers and gained 478 yards of offense. Jordan Love played out of his MIND, completing 23 of 29 for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Few teams are hotter than the Packers right now, and their defense matched their offense in New England. Green Bay did, however, lose running back Josh Jacobs to a broken finger. The Packers still have concerns, but Love is playing at an MVP rate.

Drew Lock is 2-0 this season for Seattle; he completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown in this low-scoring 17-3 win over Arizona. Seattle travels to Las Vegas to play the Raiders before going into a bye week.

The Pittsburgh Steelers were on their bye in Week 9.

The Giants continue to win football games because they're well coached in every phase. The defense pressured and harassed Joe Milton all game, sacking the young quarterback seven times, while Matt Nagy called a fine game for multiple quarterback. Jameis Winston led the only touchdown drive against Vic Fangio's defense. The Giants earned their first win in Philadelphia since 2013.

The Rams defeated Washington 20-13 on the road, but lost their star receiver Puka Nacua in the last play of the game. Los Angeles is a good team that is well coached, but injuries are stacking up, and a lack of offensive playmakers is problematic. They may receive Terrance Ferguson back soon, but Matt Stafford is losing targets weekly.

The Patriots were embarrassed by the Packers, 45-27. They're an injured squad at receiver and Drake Maye tossed three interceptions and was harassed throughout the game. It was a tough look for New England on defense – they surrendered a surprising 478 yards to Jordan Love and the Packers.

The Texans came off the bye week and blew the Chargers out, 44-22. C.J. Stroud went nuclear, finishing 21 of 35 for 384 yards with five touchdowns and a pick. Kayshon Boutte went four for 125 and two; Tank Dell four of 105 for one, and Nico Collins four for 55 with one as well. Houston played to their talent against the worst team in the league.

Cleveland lost 23-22 in overtime. Shedeur Sanders went 19 of 31 for 297 yards with two touchdowns with exceptional individual efforts from Harold Fannin Jr. and KC Concepcion on the two 64 and 39 yard touchdown passes. Tyler Shough turned it on down the stretch of the game and the Saints found a way to secure victory at the end of the game. Cleveland has a decision to make next week – Sanders or DeShaun Watson?

Tampa Bay has won two games in a row and three of four. The Bucs won last week without completing a pass. They're a power-run team with an opportunistic, well-coached defense, but the Bears withstood a valiant come-from-behind effort. Tampa Bay lost 27-24.

Baltimore lost to Jacksonville, 33-10, but they were forced to start Joe Fagnano, who went 10 of 18 for 60 yards. Baltimore had a creative game plan centered around the wildcat, but Jacksonville was too much in the second half. Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett, who should start in Week 10.

Bryce Young played well against a good defense, completing 28 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns, but as the Broncos do – they found a way to win, 26-21. The Panthers are now 3-5 with three straight losses.

The Raiders turned the football over five times, with three of them being Kirk Cousins interceptions. Brock Bowers caught seven passes for 111 yards with a touchdown on eight targets. The Raiders can't beat a team like San Francisco on the road while throwing three picks and putting the ball on the ground three more times (two of which were recovered by the other team).

Tyler Shough led a fourth-quarter comeback to force overtime and finished the game 21 of 35 for 265 yards with a touchdown and 51 yards on the ground. Audric Estime, who was on the Browns' practice squad last week, rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown for the Saints.

Atlanta has lost four of the last five games, this one in Madrid, Spain. The quarterback play is sub-par; Michael Penix Jr. threw for just 162 yards in the game, and Drake London took a bit to get going. Atlanta is in a bad division, and they're a team that struggles to establish an identity.

Dallas has talent on both sides of the football, but they're a mess. Dak Prescott, though, did complete 21 of 34 for 335 yards and a pair of touchdowns against a Colts team that is in a fire sale. Dallas, somehow, almost lost this game and found a way to win late 27-23. The Cowboys are one of the biggest disappointment teams in the 2026 season, which is just lovely.

Jayden Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards with a touchdown pass to Van Jefferson, but that wasn't enough to defeat the Los Angeles Rams, who earned this road win, 20-13. Washington's offense has struggled and the Commanders' rushing attack remained bad in this game.

The Jets went to Kansas City and lost, 35-12. They did little offensively, converting 2 of 14 third and fourth down conversions. They couldn't stop the run on defense. Aaron Glenn's time as a head coach may be coming to an end.

Gardner Minshew II couldn't do much against Mike Macdonald's defense in this 3-17 loss. Minshew was then hurt and it looks like Arizona will turn to Carson Beck, now that Jacoby Brissett was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona is down love, multiple quarterbacks, and Michael Wilson was placed on IR. Not good!

Miami played well since their bye week, but could only muster nine points against Detroit. Malik Willis finished 13 of 25 for just 128 yards with an interception. It's a rebuilding year for Miami.

The Eagles have lost seven straight games and changed to quarterback Joe Milton to try and spark the team at home against the Giants. The defense played with spirit, but the offense was inept, and the rushing attack was stifled by the Giants' defense. Philadelphia traded Jordan Davis on Monday morning, and they're looking forward to the off-season.

The Tennessee Titans wereon their bye in Week 9.

Daniel Jones almost did the Giants a solid by stealing a win in this lost season, but Dallas escaped with a 27-23 victory.

The Chargers are terrible. They can't do anything but score 13 points in garbage time to make the score more respectable. Just an embarrassing season for this franchise.
